Companion Animal Travel Desk Service Standards and Check-in Handling

This section explains how staff receive, review, and move companion animal travel cases with steady service and clear handoff.

The Companion Animal Travel Desk treats every journey as shared responsibility, so staff should keep language concise, kind, and actionable from the first contact through final transfer. When a traveler arrives with a companion animal file, staff should confirm the booking details, review the travel notes, and keep the discussion calm and direct. <<FACT F086>> After that, staff should check that the record is complete, the animal is fit for travel handling, and any required support items are listed before the case moves forward. If a detail is missing or unclear, staff should pause the process and route the matter through the normal service path rather than guess.

During review, staff should listen for mobility needs, carrier concerns, feeding notes, and arrival or transfer preferences. The desk should keep the tone respectful and avoid extra commentary. If a traveler needs a handoff to another team, the case should be summarized in plain words and kept limited to what the next team needs to continue service. <<FACT F106>> The desk should never leave a case hanging after a transfer request; staff should confirm that the handoff is set and that the traveler knows what happens next.

Records must be entered clearly, with no stray marks, no informal shorthand, and no assumptions about animal behavior or traveler intent. Staff should use the approved file path for follow-up and place any special note where the next shift can see it quickly. When a companion animal cannot be processed as presented, staff should explain the service limit in calm language and offer the next acceptable step within policy.

If the desk needs help with a live case, contact the senior coordinator or the duty lead through the standard service channel.
